text.text: Let’s verify this important theorem with a simple proof. Consider a right triangle with legs a and b, and hypotenuse c. By the Pythagorean theorem, c² = a² + b².
We can also visualize the theorem by plotting the squares on each side of a right triangle. The sum of the areas of the small squares equals the area of the largest square (hypotenuse).
Try solving for the hypotenuse if a=5 and b=12. Use the formula a² + b² = c² to calculate c. Check your answer using the graph.
